newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo militia seizes Brazzaville city centre.
newsitem.headline: Congo militia seizes Brazzaville city centre.

text.p: A Congolese militia fighting against troops loyal to the president seized the centre of Brazzaville on Sunday.
As fighting continued for a fourth day France said it would send reinforcements following threats to its nationals and the death of a French soldier.

Western military sources said militia fighters loyal to ex-president Denis Sassou Nguesso and opposed to President Pascal Lissouba had occupied most of the city centre and surrounded the prime minister's office and treasury.
"The Cobras have taken the centre of town and are heading for the town hall. They have captured a number of small armoured vehicles and light tanks from the army," one source said.
Officials at the presidency said discussions had begun with representatives of Sassou Nguesso and other political leaders, but the message had not yet reached the fighters.
"French military reinforcements will be flown to Brazzaville beginning tomorrow," French foreign ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said in a statement. He did not say how many troops were involved.

There are currently some 450 French soldiers in Brazzaville. They were sent there in March to evacuate foreigners from Kinshasa if necessary during the final days of the civil war in former Zaire that brought Laurent Kabila to power.

French troops have intervened during army mutinies in neighbouring Central African Republic, another former colony, to evacuate foreigners and restore order. They handed over in February to an African peacekeeping force.

One French soldier was killed and five others wounded in Brazzaville on Saturday as they tried to evacuate foreign residents from a building where they had been trapped by gunfire. A senior Congolese army officer working with the French soldiers was also wounded.

Doutriaux said about 100 of the 2,200 French nationals in the Brazzaville area had been taken from their homes and regrouped in safe areas because of anti-French sentiment and outbreaks of violence and looting in the capital.
A senior presidency official said a mediation committee had been set up, chaired by Bernard Kolelas, the mayor of Brazzaville and Lissouba's main political opponent.

"We've already got somewhere with the political leaders, but we are having trouble getting the message across on the ground. The thing is now for the soldiers to calm down," he said. "Some discussions have started."
He said the committee would include people from the political factions of Lissouba, of Sassou Nguesso and of Kolelas as well as members of civic groups. He said Lissouba was at the presidency.
Kolelas, whose supporters have played no part in the fighting so far, offered his mediation on Saturday.
Fighting began on Thursday after troops surrounded Sassou Nguesso's home to enforce a ban on militias following clashes in the north ahead of July 27 presidential elections.
Political parties armed their supporters during ethnic and political fighting which killed 2,000 people following disputed parliamentary elections in 1993.
Witnesses said fighting was heavy overnight, particularly around the airport. Heavy weapons fire could be heard across the Congo River in Kinshasa on Sunday.

"The problem is that there are Nguesso's militias and there are Congolese army units which are not under the control of their officers, and so we have seen Congolese troops firing on their fellow soldiers," said Commander Alexis Jaraud, the commander of French forces in Congo Brazzaville.
"There is shooting in the streets, and they are using rocket-launchers in residential neighbourhoods," Jaraud told French television LCI by telephone.
A plane carrying 44 U.S. citizens across the Congo River from Brazzaville to Kinshasa, the capital of Laurent Kabila's Congo, came under fire on Saturday.
There was no reliable death toll for the clashes although police sources spoke of several dozen dead and many wounded.
